content.title: Invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS
content.summary: Recommendations for timing and type of invasive strategy in patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes (NSTE-ACS).

recommendations.recommendation: An invasive strategy during hospital admission is recommended in NSTE-ACS patients with high-risk criteria or a high index of suspicion for unstable angina.
recommendations.notes: Applies to patients with high-risk criteria or high suspicion for unstable angina.

recommendations.recommendation: A selective invasive approach is recommended in patients without very high- or high-risk NSTE-ACS criteria and with a low index of suspicion for NSTE-ACS.
recommendations.notes: For lower-risk presentations with low suspicion.

recommendations.recommendation: An immediate invasive strategy is recommended in patients with a working diagnosis of NSTE-ACS and at least one very high-risk criterion.
criteria: Recurrent or refractory chest pain despite medical treatment
Acute heart failure presumed secondary to ongoing myocardial ischaemia
Recurrent dynamic ST-segment or T-wave changes, particularly intermittent ST-segment elevation
recommendations.notes: Immediate invasive management when any listed very high-risk feature is present.

recommendations.recommendation: An early invasive strategy within 24 hours should be considered in patients with at least one high-risk criterion.
criteria: Confirmed diagnosis of NSTEMI based on current recommended ESC high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) algorithms
recommendations.notes: Early invasive strategy recommended for higher-risk NSTEMI presentations; GRACE score threshold indicated.

abbreviations.GRACE: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events

content.footnote: ST-segment elevation equivalents are presented in supplementary data (Figure S2).
